utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Case number IT-95-16-T, the Prosecutor versus Zoran Kupreskic, Mirjan Kupreskic, Vlatko Kupreskic, Drago Josipovic, Dragan Papic, and Vladimir Santic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you. Good morning. I see that the next witness is already in, Mrs. Vidovic. Good morning, Mrs. Vidovic. Could you please make the solemn declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you. You may be seated. Counsel Puliselic?

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. We have a change for today, and Mrs. Pinter will be examining this witness. Examined by Mrs. Pinter:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good morning, Mrs. Vidovic?

utterances.speaker: ANKICA VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you tell us some general facts about you?

utterances.speaker: ANKICA VIDOVIC
utterances.text: My name is Ankica Vidovic. I was born on the 1st of December, 1957, in Busovaca. I live in Vitez and I am a hairdresser by profession.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long have you been living in Vitez?

utterances.speaker: ANKICA VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I've lived in Vitez since the 16th of April, 1993, the first day when the Muslims attacked the Croats.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And where did you reside prior to that?

utterances.speaker: ANKICA VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Prior to that, I resided in Buhine Kuce.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How far are Buhine Kuce from Ahmici?

utterances.speaker: ANKICA VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Buhine Kuce are about two -- one and a half to two kilometres away from Ahmici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how far --

utterances.speaker: ANKICA VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And they are three kilometres from Vitez.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you know Dragan Papic?

utterances.speaker: ANKICA VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I know Dragan Papic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you see him in the courtroom?

utterances.speaker: ANKICA VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you have any close contacts with him? Did you socialise with him? How long have you known him? Tell the Court, please.

utterances.speaker: ANKICA VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I have known Dragan since I married in Vitez in 1974. And when I came to live there, he was a boy. Dragan was born in 1967 and he was 7 years old at the time I came to Vitez. He was riding a bicycle and he would frequently go to Zume and the football field there, where the children used to gather, so that I got to know Dragan through my husband.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's what I wanted to ask you. Why did you go to Zume?

utterances.speaker: ANKICA VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I went to Zume because my husband was a football fan, and while he was a young man he played a lot of football and was later on a coach for Santici, the football team.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Later on you began socialising with Dragan more?

utterances.speaker: ANKICA VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that is true. When Dragan married in 1991 and he met my husband, we knew that he had got married. We asked who he had married, and he told us that he had married Rujica Lastro, her surname was Lastro. My maiden name was Lastro as well, so we thought that it might be a distant relation of mine, and that -- my husband (sic) and I called each other baja (phoen).

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, what does that mean?

utterances.speaker: ANKICA VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Well, it would mean as if -- a sort of term for sisters, as if we were sisters. But we weren't really sisters; it was just that we had this surname in common.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know whether Dragan was in conflict with anybody?

utterances.speaker: ANKICA VIDOVIC
utterances.text: No, I never heard that from anybody.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know whether he was aggressive or anything of that kind?

utterances.speaker: ANKICA VIDOVIC
utterances.text: No, he was not aggressive at all. He was very calm. He is fairly good at communicating with people. In fact, he liked communicating with everybody, and he liked having a lot of friends around him, and he had a lot of friends and we are his friends.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you socialise intensively, so that you could say -- give us these character traits for certain? Were you friends for a long time?

utterances.speaker: ANKICA VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. From 1991 onwards, we saw each other more frequently. Particularly in the summertime, at Rasko Polje, we would have barbecues, and they would visit us, we would visit them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did Dragan read a lot?

utterances.speaker: ANKICA VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I doubt it very much. I didn't often see him with a book in his hands.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did Dragan like doing outside his regular job, regular line of business?

utterances.speaker: ANKICA VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Dragan was a forester by profession, but I used to meet him most often with his hands dirty and oily, wearing a work overall, because he worked as a car mechanic. And that was his hobby, in fact.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was Dragan particularly interested in history?

utterances.speaker: ANKICA VIDOVIC
utterances.text: No, he wasn't. I don't think he was, no. We never discussed things of that kind.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was Dragan in some way politically involved? Was he a member of any party? Do you know anything about that?

utterances.speaker: ANKICA VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know that he was a member of any party, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And if he was, would you have known?

utterances.speaker: ANKICA VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I would. Quite certainly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During these days when you saw him and were friends, did he ever display his political viewpoints or take nationalist standpoints, or were these discussions never a topic that you discussed, or did you ever have any other views?

utterances.speaker: ANKICA VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Dragan never was interested in politics, nor was my husband, nor was I, so we didn't discuss things like that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Where would you meet Dragan from time to time? You said that you met him from time to time; where would that be?

utterances.speaker: ANKICA VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Well, before the war and after the war, I would meet him frequently at Fadil Cajic's, who was an auto mechanic and had his own shop by the railway station.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see him after the war as well?

utterances.speaker: ANKICA VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Dragan would go there after the war as well because I took my car there to have my oil changed and I came across Dragan.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The auto mechanic, was he a Muslim?

utterances.speaker: ANKICA VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Fadil Cajic was a Muslim living in Vitez by the railway station. He lived there throughout the war and he's still living there today and working there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us who Dragan associated with most when he wasn't, of course, with his wife and so on, if you know anything about that?

utterances.speaker: ANKICA VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Dragan worked in the Sumarija, the forestry concern of Vitez, as a forester, and he was friends with Strmonja Nermin who went to the forestry school together with him and I would often see them walking by and they would always say hello when they passed me by.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know whether Dragan went to the mosque at all?

utterances.speaker: ANKICA VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Well, he quite certainly did go to the mosque as a child because the mosque was situated across the road from his house. I can't confirm this actually but I do know that he would go to funerals just like me if a Muslim person were to die and he would attend the funeral which meant that he would go to the mosque as well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After the war, did you have further contacts with Dragan?

utterances.speaker: ANKICA VIDOVIC
utterances.text: After the war, we did associate, Dragan and Ruzica visited me after the war, Ruzica in the course of the war spent the war with her parents, she was at her parents' place.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you discuss things after the war, can you tell us what Dragan's relationship after the war was toward the Muslims?

utterances.speaker: ANKICA VIDOVIC
utterances.text: His relationship towards the Muslims after the war did not change because Dragan continued to see Muslims, associate with them, and Muslims would come to his house, to his yard, because I would have occasion to pass by his house, because our Croatian cemetery is located three houses from -- Dragan's house is the third house from the cemetery, so when I was passing by I would see Muslim's cars parked there in front of his house and in his yard which meant that Muslims came to Dragan's place.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Except for these cars parked in front of his house, can you tell us about Dragan's attitude toward the Muslims and towards the war as well?

utterances.speaker: ANKICA VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Dragan always felt sorry for everybody and for the Muslims too. He had a lot of Muslim friends who had lost their lives during the war and so he would often mention the Muslim names and say how sorry he was, particularly mentioning Nermin, who had been killed and came there as a refugee.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you talk about relations between Croats and Muslims after the war?

utterances.speaker: ANKICA VIDOVIC
utterances.text: No, I was no longer interested in that at all because I lost a great deal in the war.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you change your attitude towards the Muslims? Have you changed it after the war?

utterances.speaker: ANKICA VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I have changed my attitude, and Dragan would always give words of encouragement and say, "Well, never mind," what happened is not a good thing but we still have to continue to live together and cooperate with people, and I just couldn't do that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You lost somebody during the war, did you not?

utterances.speaker: ANKICA VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I lost a great deal during the war.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us whom you lost or don't you want to talk about it?

utterances.speaker: ANKICA VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I can tell you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I lost my husband, my son, my brother-in-law, his wife and their two children. This happened on the 9th of January when the Muslims stormed Buhine Kuce, and they all lost their lives in one single day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you discuss this matter with Dragan?

utterances.speaker: ANKICA VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, but I didn't want to discuss the matter at any length, and Dragan would always advise me and tell me that I should try and put it behind me, forgive and to continue living, that life goes on, and he would console me and say that it wasn't individual people who were to blame, just like ...

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Individual people or the nation as a nation?

utterances.speaker: ANKICA VIDOVIC
utterances.text: No, the nation as a nation was not to blame, that the ethnicity wasn't to blame, and that we were not to blame just like the Muslims were not to blame.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: That will be all. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you. Counsel Pavkovic, any cross-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. PAVKOVIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Defence Jadranka Slokovic-Glumac has a few questions to ask.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you. Ms. Slokovic-Glumac? Cross-examined by Ms. Slokovic-Glumac:

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mrs. Vidovic, good morning to you?

utterances.speaker: ANKICA VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Madam.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell us where you were working in 1994?

utterances.speaker: ANKICA VIDOVIC
utterances.text: In 1994 I was working in Vitez at the Kralja Petra Kresimira Street at the Vucjak building as it was referred to.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did you do there?

utterances.speaker: ANKICA VIDOVIC
utterances.text: As my hairdressing salon was destroyed by the railway station, I rented a space and premises from the municipality and worked as a hairdresser.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From what month were you employed as a hairdresser there?

utterances.speaker: ANKICA VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I began putting the premises in order from July, and I began intensively working since August when I returned from my holiday.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know Mirjan Kupreskic?

utterances.speaker: ANKICA VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I know him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he work next to your -- near your salon in 1994?

utterances.speaker: ANKICA VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. We were practically facing -- our windows were practically facing each other. We worked together for some two years, and we would be together every day. We would have coffee, and fruit juices and things like that together.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What shop did he work at?

utterances.speaker: ANKICA VIDOVIC
utterances.text: He worked at the Veleprodaja in Sutra.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that you had worked in his vicinity for two years?

utterances.speaker: ANKICA VIDOVIC
utterances.text: More than two years.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That means 1994 and you say 1995 and 1996?

utterances.speaker: ANKICA VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Then I returned to my own premises.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you associate with him at that time? Did you communicate with him every day?

utterances.speaker: ANKICA VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. We were together every day. We would even have coffee every day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know at that time after the war whether he went abroad at any time?

utterances.speaker: ANKICA VIDOVIC
utterances.text: He went abroad with the folklore society. He went to Switzerland in 1995, the autumn of 1995, in fact.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At that time was he ever wearing a military uniform?

utterances.speaker: ANKICA VIDOVIC
utterances.text: No. He was always very neat and tidy and wore a suit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that was his regular place of employment, of work?

utterances.speaker: ANKICA VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When asked by my colleague, you said that you had some problems with your relationship to the Muslims because your family really did suffer a great deal and you lost a lot of your nearest and dearest. Can you tell us what Mirjan Kupreskic's relationship at that time was towards the Muslims?

utterances.speaker: ANKICA VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mirjan's relationship towards the Muslims was very good, because they came, Muslims, that is, came to the shop every day and he would talk to them. He worked as a worker there, an employee. He was a cashier and would take in what people paid to them. He helped them. We didn't always agree. In fact, I didn't always agree with him, because he would try and console me and tell me that I shouldn't be like that towards the Muslims. I would even park my car and wouldn't move my car when the Muslims would come, and he would say, "Why don't you move your car? It's not in order. Let people come. It's normal and we have to live together with them."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mrs. Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: ANKICA VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you, Counsel Slokovic-Glumac. Mr. Smith? Cross-examined by Mr. Smith:

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Morning, Ms. Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: ANKICA VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Because of the events that occurred in the war, you've stated in your evidence that your attitude towards the Muslims has changed.

utterances.speaker: ANKICA VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what is your attitude towards the Muslims generally now?

utterances.speaker: ANKICA VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Well, let me put it this way: Generally speaking, I have changed too. My attitude at the beginning was a very difficult one, because I had lived through a great tragedy, I was not, quite simply, able to imagine that something like that could happen at all. But as the days are passing one by one, I see that the people, the Muslims just like we Croats, are not to blame for what happened, but, quite simply -- it's not that I hate anybody. I don't hate anybody. I won't wish for vengeance, anything like that, revenge, but I would just like the people who are responsible for the crimes be brought to justice, but we as a people, as a nation -- we as people really aren't to blame.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in 1992, do you remember the conflict in Ahmici in October?

utterances.speaker: ANKICA VIDOVIC
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You stated in your evidence that you knew Dragan Papic wouldn't be a member of a political party. Are you aware of Dragan Papic's association with the village guard in Santici and Ahmici, and his association with the HVO in 1992, before the main conflict?

utterances.speaker: ANKICA VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Well, let me tell you, as far as those parties are concerned, I don't know. If he was, he was a member of the HDZ like I was, and old ladies as Croats were members of the HDZ as Croatian ethnicity. Perhaps that. I don't know about anything else.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you're not aware of his involvement in the village guard in Ahmici?

utterances.speaker: ANKICA VIDOVIC
utterances.text: No, because Ahmici was two kilometres away from my house, one and a half to two kilometres away, so I didn't know about that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you aware that -- or did you see Dragan Papic wearing a camouflage uniform and a black uniform on different occasions in 1992?

utterances.speaker: ANKICA VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I can tell you that Dragan usually wore his work overalls because he worked as a car mechanic, so the sort of blue type of uniform. Perhaps he had a sort of black overall as well, but he was always dirty and oily because of the car repair work that he was doing. He would repair cars, and so perhaps ....

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you never saw him in a camouflage uniform?

utterances.speaker: ANKICA VIDOVIC
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How often did you meet Dragan Papic in 1992? How frequently was it?

utterances.speaker: ANKICA VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I couldn't tell you exactly, but less and less because I and my children went to Split in 1992. I was there for two months and then I returned, and then we saw less of each other.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If I can ask you this question: Between October 1992 and April 1993, did you see Dragan Papic?

utterances.speaker: ANKICA VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I saw him but rarely. I would see him rarely.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you notice a change between Croats and Muslims in your village between October 1992 and April 1993, less co-operation?

utterances.speaker: ANKICA VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I didn't really notice that because I myself as a Croat had a pupil that was a Muslim, until the last day, that is to say the 15th of April when I stopped working. I wasn't able to go to work in the morning. But Adnana Kablar, she was a Muslim and she was with me, and she was learning the trade and everything was more or less normal. Now, what people thought in their own selves I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you work in Vitez in October 1992?

utterances.speaker: ANKICA VIDOVIC
utterances.text: No. In October 1992 I was working at the railway station and I had my own private hairdressing salon there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In terms of relationships between Muslims and Croats in Ahmici, between October 1992 and April 1993, is it fair to say that you can't really comment on what those relationships were like because you didn't live there?

utterances.speaker: ANKICA VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I can say that I don't know because I wasn't there, because Ahmici is one and a half to two kilometres away from my house, so I don't know people from Ahmici, the Muslims, really well, even Croats.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On the 16th of April, '93, you were living in your house in Buhine Kuce; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ANKICA VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, I was in my own house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How did you get from your house to Vitez on that morning, on that day?

utterances.speaker: ANKICA VIDOVIC
utterances.text: On that morning I was with my children alone at home and I heard shooting. As my house -- first of all, there's my father-in-law's house, and my brother-in-law's house and mine was some 50 to 100 metres away, and my sister-in-law called me on the phone and told me to come down to hers because there was sounds of shooting. My son and my daughter and myself we were sleeping. Then we got ready and went down to their place, and there was shooting, I don't know from what direction, because my husband had left for Kuber on Tuesday, that is to say, three days previously, prior to the shooting. He was sort of an HVO reserve, home guards unit at Kuber, and he would take seven-day-shifts on Kuber. So he wasn't at home, so that I didn't know what was going on, because I worked every day and it was just that particular morning that I wasn't able to go to work. Then I went with my children to my in-law's, and my brother-in-law and his family and their two children were there too, and we didn't know where to go and what was going on and where things were happening. And first of all, we went to the Impregnacija facility and returned, but I was no longer able to go back to my house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And why were you unable to go back to your house?

utterances.speaker: ANKICA VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I was not able to go back to my house because there was shooting from all sides and from my house, the second house is Ferid Dzidic's house, a Muslim house, and there was shooting there nonstop, and many people and young girls were killed by bullets from that house, and so I could not return. So I had to seek shelter elsewhere with my children. I had a relation in Vitez, and I spent one month with her.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you said that Dragan Papic worked with Nermin Strmonja, and he used to --

utterances.speaker: ANKICA VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: -- work together; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ANKICA VIDOVIC
utterances.text: They would go back from work together. In the afternoon I would see them going back from work. I saw them together in the afternoons. Yes, Dragan went to secondary school with Nermin. Nermin is from Pirici and Dragan from Ahmici, and they went to secondary school together, and then they worked together afterwards.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you aware of a person called Nenad Santic?

utterances.speaker: ANKICA VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I know Nenad Santic. He was killed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And he was in charge of the village guard in Ahmici and Santici; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ANKICA VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I couldn't tell you that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: I have no further questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you. Counsel Pinter?

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. No further questions. Once again with the microphone on; I have no further questions. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: All right. We don't have any questions either. Mrs. Vidovic, thank you very much for giving evidence in court. You may now be released. Thank you. (The witness withdrew)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Counsel Puliselic, shall we follow the order indicated in your document you filed last week as far as witnesses are concerned, so shall we now hear witness number 5, then 6 and 7, that order?

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Yes. Zdenko Rajic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: And none of them is asking for protective measures, I gather?

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: No. As far as I know, the witnesses whom I have called have not asked for any protection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you. (The witness entered court)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Good morning Mr. Rajic. Could you please make the solemn declaration?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you. You may be seated. Counsel Puliselic? Examined by Mr. Puliselic:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Rajic, good morning.

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please introduce yourself to the Trial Chamber by stating your full name, date of birth, place of birth and place of residence?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes. I am Zdenko Rajic. I was born on 7th April, 1969 in Rijeka in Vitez municipality, and I continue to reside there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell the Trial Chamber, what is your current occupation?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes. I am a member of the Ministry of the Interior; that is, I'm a civilian policeman in Vitez.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you say where did you live in 1992 and 1993?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes, I lived in Rijeka, in Vitez municipality.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: With the assistance of the usher, please, could we temporarily remove the smaller aerial photograph. Mr. Rajic, to your right there is an aerial photograph of the Lasva Valley. Could you point in this photograph where the village of Rijeka is located, the place where you live?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes. It is right here. This is the village of Rijeka where I live.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. If you took the road, how far would Rijeka be from Vitez?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: About three kilometres.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And if you took the road to Ahmici, how far would that be? What is the distance?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: Also between three and three and a half kilometres.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In your view, what is the distance between Rijeka and Ahmici as the crow flies?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: About -- between 1.500 and 1.600 metres.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do any Muslims live in Rijeka?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes, they do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell what is the ethnic composition in Rijeka in terms of per cent? If you know.

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: There are about 70 per cent of Croats and about 30 per cent of Muslims.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you say what the relations are in Rijeka between Croats and Muslims? If you could say what they were like before the war and what they are like now.

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: Before the war, the relations were ideal. Of course, during the war, some tensions arose. And after the war, again, the good neighbourly relations were restored.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So we can conclude that even after the war, there was no great intolerance and conflicts; is that what we can conclude?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct, there were none.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you say, did Muslims at any time leave Rijeka during the conflict between Croats and Muslims in other areas?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: No, they did not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did Muslims from Rijeka take part in fighting against the Serbs? That is, at the beginning of the war.

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: No, they did not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What about Croats? Did they take part in the fighting against Serbs? And I'm referring to the Croats from Rijeka.

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes, they did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell, in what areas did they take part?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes. We covered the wider area of Vlasic, which is in the Travnik municipality, as well as Jajce and Bugojno.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you personally take part in fighting against the Serbs?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When was this, approximately? During what period?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: Approximately it was in late June 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And where was this when you personally took part in it?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: This was the wider area of Vlasic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you take part in it as a volunteer, or were you mobilised?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: I went as a volunteer.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you therefore part of the regular HVO troops, or were you part of the HVO reserves?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: I was part of the regular HVO troops.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us whether there were village guards in Rijeka?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes, they did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you also specify the time period: When were they established?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: This was sometime in June of 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did Muslims also take part in the village guards in Rijeka?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes, some of them did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So for the most part, Croats took part in it, and some Muslims; is that what we can conclude?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell, what was the purpose, what was the objective of these village guards?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: The objective of the village guards was expressly to secure the facilities which were of vital interest.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you say whether -- could you say what were such facilities in the area of Rijeka?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: Those were the bridges -- that is, the communications across the Lasva Valley -- as well as the reservoirs of drinking water.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you personally take part in these village guards?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: I did, but only once.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm going to ask you several questions relating to the conflict between the Croats and Muslims in Ahmici on the 20th of October, 1992. Do you recall where you were on 19 October, 1992; that is, on the eve of this conflict in Ahmici?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes, I recall I was in Rijeka, in front of Srecko Petrovic's house. His nickname is Tajo. And on that day, I was on duty in the regular troops.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you on duty on that day, or were you on duty that night, between the 19th and the 20th?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes, I was on duty on that night, between 7.00 p.m. until 7.00 a.m.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you were on duty with the regular HVO shift?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that you carried out your duty that night in a house; whose house was it?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes, this was in the house which was owned by Srecko Petrovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see Goran Males that evening, or that night?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did see him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did Goran Males at that time live in Rijeka?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes, he did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was Goran Males your friend?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why did he come to you? What did he tell you?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: He told me to relate what happened to him that night near Topole -- near the Topole cemetery, which was in the Ahmici area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he confide to you as a friend, or because you were a duty officer?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: He confided to me as a friend, because we had been very close from the time we were children.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So what did he tell you? What had happened to him? If you can just very briefly relate that.

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: He told me that he was in the Busovaca area, in the village of Podjele, and on the way back home he was stopped by the BH army members in the village of Topole, near the Catholic cemetery, and that he was subjected to acts of provocation and mistreatment by the BH army members.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he tell you that somebody had proposed to have him executed?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes, he heard several voices whom he did not recognise, and they were saying that they should get rid of him, that they should kill him, execute him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he perhaps tell you, how did he get out of that situation?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes, he also said that he heard a voice from the group, and he also did not recognise that voice, and this voice said that this man should be released, meaning Goran Males.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The men who had surrounded him, did they wear uniforms? Were they members of the army of Bosnia and Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: He told me that they were wearing uniforms and that they were members of the BH army.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That night, when Males came to you, was he wearing civilian clothes?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: I believe that he did, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was Goran Males a member of the HVO himself at that time?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes, he was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Concerning this incident that was related to you by Goran Males, did you inform anybody because you were the officer on duty?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did inform my commander, Karlo Grabovac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Later on during that night, while you were on duty, did anything else happen? Did somebody call you or look for you, phone you, or try to reach you by some other means?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes, I received a call.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who called you?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: It was the commander, Karlo Grabovac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What time, approximately, was it when this happened?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: This was sometime in the morning, around 5.00.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you now briefly state what your commander, Karlo Grabovac, told you?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: He told me that he had been informed that, from the direction of Busovaca and Kiseljak, a group of HVO soldiers were coming which were moving in the direction of Jajce, and because of the barricade which had been erected on Highway 5 in the village of Topole, that is near the Catholic cemetery, that I should provide security for a group of soldiers who were coming through in case it was necessary.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What time was it when you started from Rijeka on that morning? Approximately what time it was?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: It was between 5.00 and 5.10; around there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many were you in this group or in this unit, if you know how many men?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: We were twelve.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who was the commander of this unit?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: I was the commanding officer, personally.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you say which road did you take in the direction of Ahmici?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes. We started out from Rijeka towards the railroad station by taking the highway to Zume, that is to Santici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: Then we took a local road to Donja Rovna, which is to the right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you go in a vehicle?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: No. We walked down the local road.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So when you left the highway, the main road, you were on foot when going to Santici by using this local road?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes. That is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you say -- tell me what weapons you had with you?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: We had automatic rifles.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you have any communication systems to communicate with your commanders on you?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes, I had a Motorola.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can I have the usher's assistance, please, to replace the aerial photograph of Ahmici, please? Looking at this aerial photograph, can you point out to the Trial Chamber the road -- or at least the portion of the road that can be seen here which you used to get to this area, how far did you come in in the vehicle, where you left your vehicle and which road did you take on foot?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes. We were moving from the direction of Vitez. This is the highway, the main road (indicating). From the direction of Vitez all the way up to here, to Santici, Zume (indicating), and here we got out of the vehicle (indicating).

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then where did you go on foot?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: We took this local road through Donja Rovna, and arrived here where the road intersects the old railroad tracks (indicating).

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: Then we followed the railroad tracks to the left and tried to get as close as possible to the Catholic cemetery (indicating).

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. You can -- I will take you back to the aerial photograph later on. When you arrived in this area in your vehicle did you perhaps hear some shots?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes. I heard fire coming from close range and some in the distance.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So both from close range and in the distance?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell me what specifically was your task and where were you to take positions, or did your commander decide that you would take decision on where to deploy your men or did he take that decision for you?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: He let me personally find the position where we would deploy.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And where did you decide to take positions? What location did you choose?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: We deployed in the forest near the Topola cemetery.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please show on the aerial photograph the forest and the position? Where in the forest did you deploy?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes. It was this part of the forest here (indicating).

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I see. That part. Could you please speak up into the microphone, please?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes. It was this section of the forest (indicating).

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. When you drew close to the forest, or were actually in the forest, did you, apart from the shooting, hear anything else perhaps? What was said?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes. I heard loud voices coming from a sort of loudspeaker, and I think that this came from the mosque.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did you hear?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: I heard, "Allah-u-ekber. Give yourselves up Croats, you're surrounded." And this was repeated three times.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know what "Allah-u-ekber" means?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: I think it means "God is the greatest."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you sure that there was a loud-speaking device on the mosque?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes, I am. I know that it came from the mosque because it was so loud that you could hear it five to ten kilometres away.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what was the weather like that morning?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: It was foggy.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us why you had taken up position in that particular section of the forest? What was the reason for that?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: Because it was our aim to secure the left block of HVO forces moving from the direction of Busovaca, and because of the possibility of the arrival of BH army members from the direction of the villages of Gornja Rovna, Kovacevac and Pezici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are they Muslim villages?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know whether any units of the army of Bosnia and Herzegovina were located there?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did have knowledge on that score.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell me whether in the course of that morning or in the course of that day when you were in the forest, did you notice any individuals in the forest?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did. I noticed a few civilians, but I didn't particularly dwell on that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you perhaps contact these people?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: With the people in the forest? No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What were they doing there? What do you think?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: I think that they were hiding there, hiding from the shooting.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you answer the following: Was your unit -- did it engage in combat operations of any kind in the course of that day? That is to say, did you take part in any way in the conflict around the barricade?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: No, we did not, because there was no need to.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you perhaps see the barricade on that particular day?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But did you know exactly where it was located? You had that information, did you not?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did have that information as to where it was located.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you have subsequent knowledge as to the fact that in a conflict over the barricade, the Croats, the locals of Ahmici, took part?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: The locals, Croats, did not take part there, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what did you learn afterwards? Did you learn that the local Muslim population of Ahmici took part?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes, they did, because they also co-operated with the members of the BH army.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you perhaps learn later on anything about whether trenches were dug in that area, or did you not learn anything of that kind? What do you know about that question?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes, I learnt that they had dug in there and around the Catholic cemetery as well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you perhaps know anything about whether anybody was killed on the occasion?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know whether any houses were damaged or destroyed?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes. I had heard that some houses had, in fact, been damaged or destroyed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know Mehmed Ahmic?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: I have heard about Mehmed Ahmic but I don't know him enough. I know that he was a higher-ranking person in the SDA party in the Vitez municipality.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you mean to say that he was a senior officer in that party? Is that what you wanted to say?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes. That's what I wanted to say, a high-ranking officer in the SDA party.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you have any knowledge as to what happened to his house on that particular day?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: Well, I learnt later that that house was hit with a shell from the Hrasno region and that the house was hit and destroyed. It was hit in the roof area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you learn anything about that house?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes, that there was ammunition there, MTS, materiel and technical devices.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you had information that in his house he held ammunition?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes, that he held that there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember whether the fog lifted on that day? You said there was fog in the morning. What happened later on in the course of the day, if you can remember?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: I remember that there was heavy fog in the morning, and in the course of the day the fog lifted, and at the end of the day it became cloudy and it began to rain.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let us now go back once again to the morning hours when you arrived in the area. When you with your group of soldiers approached Ahmici, that is to say when you were moving along the former railway lines and tracks, did you meet anybody, that is to say, before you reached the forest?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did. I met a group of women, children, and elderly people and there was the forester amongst them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did they tell you where they were going?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes. They said they were moving towards Donja Rovna.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why were they going towards Donja Rovna? Why were they going to Donja Rovna especially?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: Because there was no fighting in Donja Rovna where they were going, so they wanted to protect themselves.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that among that group of women and children you saw the forester. Who was the forester?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: The forester was Mr. Dragan Papic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: "The forester". Was that a nickname? Who called him "the forester"? Did people call him "the forester" or what?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes, we, from Rijeka, referred to him as "the forester."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long have you known Dragan Papic?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: I've known him since our school days, because we went to the same school.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you have occasion to see him after your school days?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know where he was employed?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes. He was employed at the Sumarija, or forestry, in Kruscica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us where the head office of that forestry organisation was located? Where was its head office? Where was the Sumarija head office?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: It was at Rijeka, next to the Bor restaurant.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see Dragan Papic at Rijeka?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did, because he would go there on his way to work.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know how long Dragan Papic was employed at the Sumarija or forestry?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: I think up until the beginning of the war.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let us go back once again to the meeting on the former track or line, railway line. Can you indicate on the aerial photograph of Ahmici the position that you met the group of women and children, amongst whom was Dragan Papic as well? Can you show us that location approximately?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes, I can. The meeting took place exactly here -- approximately, not exactly (indicating).

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So there were no railway lines or tracks there?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. We moved away from the railway line and were moving towards the forest.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. You may resume your seat. Do you remember whether you perhaps talked to Dragan Papic on that occasion?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you talked to him, did this group of women and children continue along their route, or did they also stop?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: They continued along their way, and I remained a little time with Dragan.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember, perhaps, how Dragan Papic was dressed on that particular occasion?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he have on that occasion any weapons, weapons of any kind?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: I am certain that he did not have any weapons.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us in a few sentences what you talked about with Dragan Papic on that occasion? Did he tell you where he was going?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes, he did. He said he was going somewhere towards Donja Rovna. And that he had received information when the shooting broke out that he was to take over a mortar, M-16 millimetre mortar of some kind. I think that's what it was. But I don't remember who he was supposed to take this over from.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he tell you, or perhaps did you ask him, what he was going to do with that small mortar, the 16-millimetre mortar?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes. He said that he would be signalling with the mortar if the forces of the BH army started moving from the direction of Kovacevac to Gornja Rovna and Pezici, towards the barricade, that is, to help the BH army.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So he was to send out signals to those who had sent him there; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you happen to ask Dragan Papic where he had learnt to handle this small mortar?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did ask him, and he said that he had learnt to handle it in the JNA; that is to say, when he did his service in the former Yugoslav People's Army.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you perhaps happen to ask him how come that mortar was in the -- small mortar was in the village?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did ask, and he said that somebody had brought it in from Slimena, along with some other weapons.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What happened in Slimena?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: Well, Slimena, that was where the former JNA barracks were, or warehouse.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know whether Slimena fell, and who took control of Slimena?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: Well, joint forces, the Croats and Muslims, I think, and it fell -- that is, it was taken over by the JNA, in August or September, if I remember correctly, and anybody who wanted to took weapons from there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that with your unit, you were stationed in the forest, in Ahmici?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes, I was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us whether in the course of that day, from the direction of Donja Rovna, you heard mortar fire?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Had there been fire of this kind, would you have heard it?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes, I would have heard it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us how long you remained with your unit at your positions in the forest that day?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: I stayed there until 4.00 p.m.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was the HVO from Busovaca and Kiseljak, had it succeeded in removing the barricade from the road?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did they move on further along the road?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When did the shooting around the barricade stop that day? What time, approximately? Can you tell us?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: I think it was about 3.30 p.m.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the course of that day, did you have any links with your commander, Grabovac? Any communication?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes, several times. By Motorola.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did your commander, Grabovac, ask you, perhaps, to intervene and to join in the conflict?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why not? Why did he not ask you to do this?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: Because there was no need to.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that you were in the forest until about 16.00 hours, if I remember correctly; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. Until about 16.00 hours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And where did you go after that? Did you take the same road that you had come, the same route, or did you take a different route?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: We did not take the same route but took the Radak Bridge route. We went on foot.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you perhaps meet Dragan Papic again that day?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: I should like the usher to come up and hand this to the witness, the Court.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The document is D28/5.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Rajic, this is the same aerial photograph that you saw up on the board, but the scale is smaller. Would you take a red Magic Marker and place the photograph on the ELMO so that everybody can see on their screens, and I should now like to ask you to take your red marker and indicate the route you took from Vitez by road. So use your red marker and draw the road you took and where you went.

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: (Marks).

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Now mark in, with the number "1," put a "1" where you got out of the vehicle.

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: (Marks).

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And parallel to the road, place an arrow so we know the direction you were moving in. So put a few arrows in.

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: (Marks).

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's right. Thank you. Now place the number "2" to denote the place you met the group of women and children and where you talked to Dragan Papic. Indicate that with the number "2."

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: (Marks).

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Put a number "3" where your position was, the position you took up with your unit in the forest.

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: (Marks).

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And number "4," the spot where, according to your knowledge and the information you received, the barricade was located which is around which the conflict took place.

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: (Marks).

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. On that particular day, did anybody -- perhaps one of your soldiers from your unit, or anybody else -- shoot from the forest in which you were located?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Had there been any shooting, would you have heard it?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes, I would have.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you have heard shooting -- let me reformulate that question: Did you perhaps on that day have any knowledge that next to the -- that a PAT was located next to the forest, a semi-automatic anti-aircraft gun? Or anybody else there?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: No, where I was, there were no -- nothing of that kind. But I did know that a PAT, a semi-automatic gun, was positioned at the place of Hrasno.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How did you know that? Did you hear any shooting from that direction? How did you know that?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: Well, I did hear shooting and I did know that detonation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: For purposes of the record, may we introduce the direction from which you heard the PAT, the anti-aircraft gun shooting. You mentioned a place but it didn't go into the --

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: The place was Hrasno. It is the Busovaca municipality, above Nadioci, near Ahmici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I should now like to ask you --

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Mr. President, perhaps it's time to take a break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Yes, we will take a 30-minute break now.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Rajic, let me ask you several questions regarding village guards. Could you tell me whether the village guards in the village which you know, that is in the Vitez municipality territory, were part of some military organisation? That is, did the military structures have any authority over the village guards?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: No. No, they did not. At least not until the war, because these were self-organised groups of villagers which gathered on their own initiative and reached their own agreements. They would choose one among themselves who would be in charge of who was going to go to guard duty, what weapons they were going to carry and what their shifts were going to be.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you said that the military structures had no influence over the organisation or command of these village guards up until the war, but what happened when the war broke out?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: When the war broke out the majority of those who were involved in the village guards started being mobilised, and, of course, they fell under the authority of the military powers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So they were registered as members of the reserve with the defence department, just as everybody else was members of the reserves. Then when they were mobilised they were then incorporated into the units of the HVO; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes, they were members of the reserve force.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know anything about mobilisation? When the conflict started was everybody mobilised right away or did this mobilisation proceed gradually?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: At the beginning of the war it proceeded in a gradual manner, of course.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us, did members of the village guards wear uniforms?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: Very few had them, and even those who had them did not have a full uniform. For instance, one would have a jacket but no pants, and jackets did not have an insignia and so on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What about the weapons of the village guards? Do you know anything about what types of weapons they had?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: I know for the most part they had hunting rifles, double barrelled, and old rifles like M-48.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: M-48, those were the old type of military rifles; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes. That is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you know, how did they acquire those rifles? Did people just find different ways to acquire them or did they come from Slimena?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: As I mentioned previously, everybody went up to Slimena and took whatever they could, and most people took rifles and took hand grenades, things like that. I think for the most part, all of these weapons came from Slimena.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could some of these weapons have been taken in combat against the Serbs and then sold? Would you say that there were cases when that occurred too?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes. That is possible, but it was rare that somebody would buy these weapons.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. I'm now going to ask you several questions relative to the second conflict between Croats and Muslims which took place on the 16th April, 1993. Can you tell us where you were on 16 April, 1993, in the morning hours?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: I was at home asleep.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And on the 15th of April, the day before, were there any indications? Did you see or hear anything that would indicate to you that on the 16th of April this type of conflict could take place?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where were you on the 15th of April?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: Also at home.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you have a day off, were you on vacation, if you were there -- if you were at home on that day too?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes, I had a day off.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what happened on 16 April in the morning? Did you hear shooting? When was it? Can you tell us a little bit more about that?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: As I said, I was asleep, and sometime between 5.00 and 5.30 I was awakened by shooting and by explosions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you perhaps talk to somebody after that? Did you meet somebody? What happened?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes, I received a telephone call.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who called you and what did you talk about?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: I was called by Karlo Grabovac, and he told me that a new conflict had broken out in Ahmici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Karlo Grabovac was your commander; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes. He told me to get -- to come out immediately and go to feature 517, which was called Crveno Brdce, which was right up from my house about 200 to 300 metres.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you now please point this position on the aerial photograph, and if I can just ask the usher's assistance to again remove the smaller aerial photograph of Ahmici. Would you please find this feature which you mentioned, Crveno Brdce?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: It is this area (indicating). This is the feature 517.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is this high ground?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes. And we had to watch and see that the Muslim forces would not advance from the area of Vranjska, which was a purely Muslim area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. You may sit down again. At this feature called Crveno Brdce, was a line of defence established there?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that you were tasked with watching that BH army forces would not advance. From which direction did you say?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: From the direction of Vranjska.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At this feature, near and around that feature, was there any significant facility located there, of some significance for Rijeka?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes. This is where reservoirs of drinking water are located, which are used by the village of Rijeka.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see Goran Males at this line of defence?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you fully established this line of defence, could you say how many of you were there at this line?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: We were about 130.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you say how long this line was? What was its length? How much space did it cover?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: About 4.000 metres, or four kilometres.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How much time did you spend there? How long did you hold this line of defence, can you recall that?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: Until the end of the war. That is, until the truce was signed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Apart from the fact that on that day, 16 April, 1993, you heard shooting and perhaps saw some smoke, because I assumed that you could see Ahmici from there, did you know on that day what actually happened in Ahmici on that day? Did you know this?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: On that day I didn't know anything except that there was fighting there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you could hear shooting, is that correct, and could you see some smoke? Yes?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes. You could see smoke and shooting could be heard.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So all this could be seen from the position in which you were located?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes, it could be seen.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you say what you learned subsequently regarding what happened in Ahmici?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: Subsequently I learned that there were a number of killed Muslims, burnt and destroyed houses, and also that there were several Croats who were killed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you learn who took part in this conflict, whether the BH army was also involved in it, the army of Bosnia and Herzegovina and the HVO? In other words, did the BH army take part in this?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did people talk about it? I'm not saying that you have any personal knowledge, but did you subsequently hear from people in conversations?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes, later on, subsequently I heard that there were armed groups of Muslims and Croats. Now, whether this was BH army and HVO, I don't know the exact names of units involved.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know that the traffic along the main Busovaca/Vitez road was blocked?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes, it was blocked at Buhine Kuce.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In what way?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: There was machine-gun fire at Buhine Kuce on the part of the BH army; that is, on the part of Muslims.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was the traffic interrupted for a day only, or did it take longer?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: This continued for the most part of the war.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what was your knowledge, given that the traffic in that part of the road was interrupted? Where was the traffic diverted from Vitez to Busovaca, and the other way around?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: If you went from Busovaca to Vitez, you would turn off to go towards Donja Rovna.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You would have to go to the left?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct, you would have to go to the left, to Gornja Rovna, then cross the Radak Bridge and go to the village of Rijeka, and on in the direction of Vitez.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. So it's through Rijeka and across Radak Bridge upstream to Rijeka; and then from Rijeka, where did you go from Rijeka? Did the road merge with the main road after Buhine Kuce?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes. Then you would reach the main road and turn left and go towards Vitez.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In light of what you have just said, did this Radak Bridge have any strategic significance, and was it to be protected?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: Absolutely. It absolutely had significance. It was the only way to Busovaca via Nadioci.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So if there is no bridge and if the road was cut off, would you have been completely cut off there?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was the danger with respect to Radak's Bridge? Why was it to be protected? From whom was it to be protected? Who could have destroyed it?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: We were to protect it from the sabotage units of the BH army, who could have destroyed it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In those wartime days, did you see or meet Dragan Papic?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: No, I did not. I only saw him after the war.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you only saw him after the end of the war; can you tell me where you saw him?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: In the town of Vitez itself.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you perhaps talk about who was where, what had happened? Did he tell you where he was during the war?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes, he did. He said that he was at first part of security of the bridge.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Which bridge is this?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: It's the Radak's Bridge. And that sometime during the war, I think it was in the fall --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Fall of which year?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: Fall of'93, he was wounded. But I don't know at which section of the defence line.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that you used to see Dragan Papic in Rijeka before the war. He was a forester there; he would come to Rijeka because that's where the administrative office of the company was. Can you tell me, did you notice anything particular on his face?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, he had a big beard.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In this courtroom, do you see Dragan Papic?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is he still wearing a beard?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes, but now it's much shorter.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So before, it was what?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: Oh, yeah, he had a much bigger and more grown-in beard.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have you heard of a unit called 92nd Vitez Home Guard Regiment?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did hear about it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From what you know, where and when was this 92nd Vitez Home Guard Regiment established? Approximately when and where was it established?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: I believe that it was established in 1994, and it replaced Vitez Brigade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
