utterances.text: I see. So it replaced Vitez Brigade; and as such, was it established after the truce was signed, or was it established before?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes, it was established after the truce was signed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So given its name, was this an active or a reserve formation?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: The very name, home guard, implies it was a reserve unit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you absolutely sure that this unit did not exist in 1992?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: 100 per cent.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you have any personal recollection that in units where you were a soldier, that you belonged to, was barred from passing on some roads by barricades set up by the BH army units?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes, I personally experienced that. I believe that this was sometime in September 1992, in the village of Karaula, which I believe is in the Travnik municipality.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where were you going at that time? Where was your -- what was the destination that your unit was trying to get to?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: Whenever we were going to Jajce, that is -- we used to go to Jajce, and we always had to go through Karaula.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So BH army units barred your passage; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes, that is what happened.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you know what kind of fighting was going on in Jajce, between whom?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: Between JNA, that is the Serbian forces, and the HVO. And of course --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who held Jajce at that time? And who was trying to take it?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: It was controlled by the HVO. And the Serbian forces wanted to take it, and then eventually they did.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: May I ask the usher's assistance to show the witness Prosecution number 353.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Rajic, in the past few days we looked at this list, and it is Prosecution Exhibit 353. From that list, as far as you recall, can you see when it was compiled, when the list was compiled? For example, on the last page, page 109, page 109, that's where the list ends. So there, or somewhere up in front, is there a date which could tell us when this list was compiled?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: No, I can't see it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Going on to the next page, there's no number there. Once again the list has been prolonged, and then the last number there is 4.653, on the next page. So the page -- the last enumerated page was 109. Turn to the next page, the page after that.

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: I can't see the number.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have you found page 109? Have you found it? At the top, in handwriting, 109, across the middle. In the middle of the page. It's not the last page. The centre top. Have you found page 109? In the centre.

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, find page 109.

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: There's nothing here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We found 109 now. Well, on that page 199 where the list was concluded, is there any date at all from which we could deduce when the list was compiled? Can you see any date there?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now turn to the next page.

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: Backwards or forwards?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Not backwards, forwards. There's no number at the top of that page, is there?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, that list was completed at the end and the last number is 4.653. Can you see a date there from which we could deduce when the list was compiled?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From this document -- take a look at the document please. At the top of this page it says -- what does it say, that these are members of -- a list of members of ...

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: The 92nd Home Guard Regiment of Vitez.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said, and here you could see the time when they were engaged in units, "From/to." Look at the date "From/to," the time they were engaged, and there are a lot of 1992 dates. At that time did the Vitez Home Guard Regiment exist?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: No, it did not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I should now like to ask you to open the document to page 82. Find page 82 now, please.

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: I've found it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the middle of the page under number 4.466, I don't know if you can see that number because --

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: I can't see that number.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You can't see it. It's in the centre of the page and your name is listed there, Zdenko Franjo Rajic.

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: I found that, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now turn to the column where it says "Status" at the top of the column.

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: I found it, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What, in your assessment, do these letters "RVI" stand for that you see at the top, "RVI"?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: It means a military invalid, wartime military invalid.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what is the letter "P" there?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: It is "reserve," Pricuva.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Your name in that column and status, you have the letter "P" where status is concerned, and then a date, followed by a date, the date you were involved, 8th of April, '92 until the 26th of February, '96, and then there is a signature. Is that your signature?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you in the reserve formation or the active component?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: I was the active component.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is the date the 8th of April, '92, the date there, does it correspond to the time that you were engaged?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: No, it does not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When were you engaged?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: I think it was about the 19th or 20th of June, 1992, but not the 92nd Vitez Home Guard Regiment but the reserve formation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you signed this did you think that it was all right to quote this earlier date?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why did this agree with you? Why did you find it all right?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: Well, because of the units (sic) themselves.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What does that mean? What did the -- I've been warned that it wasn't entered into the transcript correctly, the dionica.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Yes, indeed. I mean, "shares" has been translated as "units." "Shares," yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: "Shares." It should be "shares."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Being engaged in the war or your more years of service, did they bring you more shares, more shares to these people?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes, of course. If you had a longer time inscribed and had you been a member of a unit for a longer period of time, you would have had more shares.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was that the case with the Muslims as well?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On this list and this particular page, in your particular case -- I'm sorry that you can't see the number by the side, it would be easier to make ourselves understood if you could, but there is the name. For example, in the tenth line from the top, tenth line from the top, there is a name Koroman Ante Ivana. Is that a woman, a female name, judging by the name?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Then two lines below that there is Santic Ivo Jozuka. And then down below that we come to the end of the list, fourth line from the bottom, and there was Kalinic Ante Katica.

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes, I found that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Then two lines up above there is Frljic Milka Lucija?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are they all women?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were women members of the HVO?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now take a look at the column with the heading "JMBG." Do you know what "JMBG" stands for?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do know. The first two numbers --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Take your own, for example. Take your own JMBG and explain to the Trial Chamber what "07" represents.

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: 07 is the day of birth, then 04 is the month of birth, and 969 means the year of birth, and the left -- the numbers after that, 193628, that is the municipal number under which I am registered in the records.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Let us now go four lines below your number, and you will find Santic Franjo Franjo. Did you -- have you found that name?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What year was that individual important?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now move down seven lines below that figure, Livancic Ivo Anto. That is the name. Have you found that name?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes, I have found it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What year was that individual born in?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now look four lines down from that name -- it seems that the transcript has recorded my question as being when that lady was born -- why that date is important, and I asked when was the lady born, when was -- it's not a lady, it's a man. "When the man born," that was my question. "Santic Franjo, when was he born?" And this brings us to the name Biletic Jozo Vinko. When was he born? Four lines below Livancic Anto.

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: Biletic Jozo Vinko, he was born on the 6th of October, 1935.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: These individuals, they are men. In view of the years they were born in, could they have been members of the HVO?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: No, because they are too old to be that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Let us go back to the beginning, and let us take page 2. Have you found page 2? Line 3 there is Maros Franjo Nada.

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in the column, the number of the month before, it says "49" before the signature. So from this list would transpire that Maros Franjo Nada -- is that a woman?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That she was in the HVO for 49 months, and the same -- there is a similar thing in the next lines. Palavra Stipo Marica see, Grabovac Fabijan Ljiljana; are they women?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And it states that they were in the HVO for 37 months. Were women members of the HVO?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: No, they weren't. That was impossible.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Look at the centre of the page. It is number 51, but you can't see it because the document has been bound that way. Markovic Nikola Danica. Markovic Nikola Danica?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: I've found it, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And it says here that she was in the HVO for 49 months. Under the column where it states "Months," the figure is 49.

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes, I can see that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that possible?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the third line from the bottom it says Rajic Jozo Ljubica. Is that a woman?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Turn to page 3. Turn the third page over. In the centre and the number is 90, I can see the number as well now, and it says Majstorovic Mijo Dragana. Is that a woman?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then under 110, 111, 112, 13, it says Ruzica, Zorica, Gordana? Are they women?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes, they are.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On page 4, the column headed "JMBG," number 154, at the end of the page, third line from the bottom.

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: I've found it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And it is Milicevic Franjo Ivica. When was that individual born?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Individuals born then, could they have been members of the HVO?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: At no events, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Look at page 6. The second individual, Zahirevic Ramo Began. What year was that individual born?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now take a look at some ten lines after that, Zuljevic Jozo Anto?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes, I've found it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What year was that individual born in?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. There are other dates like that of elderly people and while we're on this page, look at line 3, please, and the name is Kolak Niko Kata.

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Then two lines below that Tomic Stipo Ana. Have you found that? Two lines below.

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes I've found it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Then we have, five or six lines below that, Samija Stipo Andelka.

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then five lines below that Sucic Nikola Sanja?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: There seems to be a problem, Mr. President, because the names have not been introduced into the transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: We will see to it that they're recorded.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Then take a look at the next line. Hrvac Slobodan Sanja?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And look down, below six or seven lines below that, Kolak Marko Dragana.

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: I've found it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are they all women?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes, they are.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: For example, on page 7, and the number is 270, it is about ten lines from the bottom, Safradin Jakov Ivo. And look at the JMBG. When was that individual born?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: Safradin Ivo was born in 1929.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What does it mean on this page, the column titled "status"? What does "PG" mean, in your assessment?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: Poginula osoba, that is killed individual.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Mr. President, there are a lot of pages, and that I know I would be taking up much too much time. I can go page by page in this way and prove that in the -- the list includes elderly individuals and a lot of women. I am not going to take up your time, but I'm just going to look at two more pages, just two more pages. So I'm going to skip the rest and I ask the witness to look at page 76.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Rajic, have you found page 76?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes, I have.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Take a look at the tenth line from the bottom. It says "Tuco Osman Ufeta."

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: I've found it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know that -- is it a woman?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know her?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: I know her personally.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is she a Muslim?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where does she live?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: At Rijeka.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What does she do?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: Well, she was a midwife.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the column, JMBG, it states -- what year was she born?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the column as to month, it says 22; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was Tuco Osman Ufeta a Muslim, therefore, and she helped women give birth, was she a member of the HVO?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm just going to look at one more page; otherwise we could spend five days going through this list. On page 94. Have you found page 94?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes, I have.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Take a look at the fourth line.

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes, I've found it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Nevanka Vinko Rajic. Do you know that person?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who is she?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: It is my bride -- that is to say my brother's wife; my brother's wife.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was she a member of the HVO?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Rajic, I won't go on with the list. What is your opinion -- you have seen the lists in quite a lot of detail; what do you think about the authenticity of this list? Is what is written here correct, or not?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: Well, this was written because of the shares that I mentioned earlier on. And the shares themselves. I know that we were to have received these shares, we Croats, just like the Muslims, for remuneration, wartime reparation. And the dates testify to the fact that they would stipulate earlier periods, earlier mobilisation, when they joined the units, whether they were active or not was not important, but that earlier dates were stated.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. But you see that there are a lot of individuals who are elderly persons; did those people take part in the war at all, and were they members of the HVO?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: No, they did not take part. But they were nonetheless included in the list.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What happened to the women? Was that the same reason? Did it apply to the women as well?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes, the reason was the same with the women because of the numerical state itself, the number of members of the HVO with respect to the number of BH army members.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So the number -- so many have been listed because of the shares; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: Quite precisely that, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President; I have no further questions. Thank you. I should like to tender into evidence the list, Defence Exhibit D28/5.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Any objections? No? It will be tendered in as evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAVKOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. President, no other Defence counsel will examine this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Terrier?

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Cross-examined by Mr. Terrier:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Rajic. My name is Franck Terrier; I'm one of the Prosecution attorneys. I'm going to ask you to answer several questions. First of all, you said at the beginning of your testimony that you are currently a policeman, a member of the civilian police in Vitez; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you specify how long it's been that you've been a policeman?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: From 21 June 1994.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What training did you receive as a policeman?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: I'm just a regular policeman.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Doesn't a regular policeman receive any training in Vitez?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: We just had a course which we took to become a policeman.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did you do before the beginning of the war? What was your position from 1990 to around the middle of 1992, what was your profession?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: I was a carpenter by trade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You told us that during the war you were a volunteer soldier. Could you tell us exactly from what point on you were a volunteer soldier in the HVO, and until what date?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: I don't know the exact date, but I believe that it was mid-June of 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And until what date did you remain a volunteer soldier?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: I was a volunteer during the period when we were fighting Serbs, and when we were -- during the conflict in early 1993, we were mobilised down at the Vitez municipality.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us, in terms of months and dates, until what date it was that you remained a soldier in the HVO ranks, volunteer soldier?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: I didn't quite understand the question, I'm afraid.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I wanted you to tell us, Mr. Rajic -- that is, to tell the Tribunal -- until what date, in terms of months and years, you were a volunteer soldier within the HVO ranks.

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: Until the beginning of the conflict in 1993. We continued fighting, but as I said, we were then assigned to this unit after this new conflict broke out.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I would like to know exactly what unit you were a member of as an HVO volunteer. What was your unit?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: It was the regular HVO, or active HVO forces.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I understood that you were a member of an active HVO unit, but could you give us more details? What unit was that, in respect of battalion, or company, or platoon?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: I just said that it was called the regular or active HVO forces of Vitez. There was no other name.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was your rank in the unit?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: It was squad commander.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us, what was the chain of command that you reported to?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: Could you please repeat the question?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us who the commander was above you who was authorised to give you orders?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: My commander was Mr. Karlo Grabovac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And above him, above Mr. Grabovac, who was it?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: I don't know. Believe me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was Mr. Grabovac's rank?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: I wouldn't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: To which units -- or over which units, rather did Mr. Grabovac command?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: The regular or active forces of the HVO, Vitez. But not all of the forces; just the ones in Rijeka.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me ask the question in a different way: How many men did Mr. Grabovac have under his command?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: I believe around 30.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Rajic, let's go back to this book for a few moments, the book that you've got in front of you, and specifically page 82, where your name appears as indicated a little while ago.

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: I've found it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. On the next-to-the-last column on the right, is your signature there?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I would like to understand the explanations that you gave a little while ago. As regards this book, was it not a logbook that had been set up in order to calculate the actions that each of the members of the HVO did? Is that the meaning of this book, this log?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: Most likely it is, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let's go back to the line which deals with you. The two dates which appear there and the number of months that you spent within the HVO; where do those numbers come from? Where do these indications come from?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you signed this log, do you remember whether those indications that were typed in respect of the dates and those that were hand-written in respect of the number of months, were these indications already there?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes, they had been entered already.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does your signature therefore confirm the reality of or the correctness of these indications?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: No. Because in those two months, I think I have more entered in than I actually did. But I was of course happy about this signature, because it meant more shares.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I think that we agree, the signature -- you said that there was an error in the book, but the signature means that you agreed with the dates that appear in the log and the number of months that have been used in order to calculate the number of shares?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes, as I said, I agreed with this, even though it is incorrect. But I agreed with it because of the shares, because of the value of shares. In other words, if you have been active for a longer period of time, you received more shares.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Therefore you received -- what you tell us, Mr. Witness, that you received more shares than you were supposed to?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You received more shares than the number of shares that you were entitled to?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could I ask you if that is correct?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: No. No, but I signed for this number of shares, just as everybody else here did, because as I said, the longer of the period of time active in the military, the more shares you received.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If I've understood the explanations which you gave us about the questions that were asked by the attorney, all people of a certain age -- middle age people signed this and all the women who signed this book, and there were some of those as well, they all signed indications that in fact are not truthful.

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct. Women and elderly men had never been mobilised in the HVO, but they were included in the list because of the shares; that is, to increase the number of shares.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Therefore, if we follow your explanations, and that's what I'm doing, all the elderly people and the women who signed this book were just as dishonest as you were. That's what you're saying, is it not?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: Honesty was not at issue here. What was at stake here was to match the number of shares which the BH army members were getting.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I don't understand your answer. Could you be more clear, please?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: By including the names of elderly and women in this list as if they had been mobilised, meant increasing the number of people receiving shares.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. What is the relationship with the compensation that was received by the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: Because of the fact that there were many more, we -- and they received many more shares. We tried to get as close to that number, to increase the number, to match their numbers, so that when these shares were distributed, that we would get as close to the number that they were getting.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why did some people receive compensation for 46 months, I think that was your case, whereas others received it for 7 months or 16 months or five months; I'm look at the page which is open in front of you. What did this correspond to?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: I don't know, because I didn't do this. There were teams of people who came to work on this, so I wasn't involved, and I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And your opinion, on what basis did the people who prepared this list base what they did?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: There's no document relating to that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You've got no record or any kind of military document or a file for each of the HVO soldiers?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: As far as I'm concerned, I had no document of that kind.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In your opinion, as far as you know, were there offices which were part of the HVO and in which records were kept or documents, case files? In respect of people who had been mobilised or who were regularly working for the HVO or in the HVO?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: I believe that after the war, such an office was established.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But when you speak about the HVO, what are we referring to? What is referred to? Does this mean that the HVO did not include administrative departments, or logistical departments, or departments that were responsible for supplies, communications, transport, and many other activities?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Within these departments that were not involved in the fighting but which were part of the HVO, was it possible that women or middle-aged people might have worked?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: No. Not elderly. At any rate, not elderly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But women?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: Some of them, but it was a rarity.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: I'm sure you have many questions, Mr. Terrier, perhaps we might take a break now for about 15 minutes?

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Yes, of course, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Witness, in order to correct an ambiguity that I see in the transcript, you confirmed that within the HVO there were logistics, supply, communications and transport services as well as others that were not directly involved in the fighting in the field; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you told us that some women -- I would like to have some more details about that -- that some of these -- some could fight in the non-combatant departments?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did say that some of them did. Perhaps like in the kitchen they would cook food, but this was infrequent.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You believe that the women were used only in the kitchen in the HVO and not, for example, in offices, or in medical departments, or other more active services, if I could say it that way, more active than that one?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: As I said, I was on a line of defence at Crveno Brdce and I did not visit offices, but I know that several ladies worked in the kitchen, they cooked there, and I did not know about the offices.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Excuse me. Mr. Rajic, you're telling us that very few women worked within the HVO but you're also saying that you didn't go to the offices and you didn't know who was working there. I'd like to have some details, more trustworthy details than you've given us up to this point. Do you know who worked in the offices?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you don't know whether they were women working there or not, that is, in the offices?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: I don't know, and had they worked there I think that I would have heard about it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: With the assistance of the usher, I would like D18/2 be shown to the witness. Mr. Rajic, this is a document which was tendered by the Defence. I would like you to turn to page 11. You have to count them because they're not numbered. Page 11 starting with the first one in the Serbo-Croatian version. Have you found the page? Could you look at line 12? Look at the numbers. There's a number on the page.

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: I -- I have -- I'm reading page 1 in the upper right corner.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. Do you see your name on line 12?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: No. No, not in this -- on this sheet. I have Jukic Dragan listed as number 12.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: The problem, Your Honours, is that the pages in this document are not numbered. Perhaps --

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes, I found it. I found it here. It was on another page.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Line 12. Line 12 and the next one is your name. Could you look at the extreme right column on the page?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What does it mean, that column?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: It states the time spent with the HVO.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What's the date that corresponds to your name?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: 4 April, '92.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Will you look at the top of the page? Can you tell us what was the date that this document was drafted?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: 27 February, 1993.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you see the 27 February, '93? On that date were any shares supposed to be given out to all of the HVO members?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: I did not understand what year you meant.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: -- 27th of February. On that date were people concerned about the shares that were to be distributed to each of the HVO members?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: No, I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The date next to your name is April of 1992, could you tell us what its meaning is, what that date means?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: I don't know, but it doesn't look right to me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'd like you to look at the next to last column starting from the left of that document. Could you tell us what that means?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: I'm afraid I don't understand you. Could you please repeat the question?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Starting from the right side of the page there is an initial column with the date, the entry -- when one entered the HVO. Then there's another column. What does the last column refer to?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: It says "sniper," which is impossible.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you're telling us that in respect of your name, we see the word "sniper" is indicated?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What do the other words next to the various names of the people on this page, what do they refer to?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: I really don't know, believe me. I know that as far as I'm concerned, this is not right at all.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What does the word "Strelac" mean?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: That means that he's an infantryman.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. An infantryman. Let me say for the Trial Chamber that the English translation of this document, which was attached to the document which had been -- disclosed by the Defence, is -- one, I can't tell you what the page number is because it's not on there, but I don't think that would be -- but it would be difficult -- it would not be a problem if you try to find the English translation again. Therefore, if we look at this document that was drafted on the 27th of February, 1993, according to what is written on the top and to the right, it appears that you were taken into the HVO in April of 1992 as a sniper. Can we say that these indications are correct?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In your opinion, why were these words put down on this document, this document which was disclosed by the Defence?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I would like to ask you now, Mr. Rajic, to look at two pages further towards the beginning of the document, that is to go to page 9. Do you see the name which is next to the number 8?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes, I see. "Dragan Papic."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What is the date which you can see in the right column?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: Just a moment, please. 23 June, 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In your opinion, is this a correct date?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: I believe it is not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why do you think that the date is not correct?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: Because I personally know that Mr. Papic worked in Sumarija as a forester until the beginning of the conflict in '93.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What is the specialisation indicated next to Mr. Papic's name in the next to last column?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: Courier.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What is that position, that specialisation? What does that mean?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: I don't know what you're referring to by saying, "What does it consist of," so I'm not clear on the question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What does a courier do specifically?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: I believe he delivers mail.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Distributes mail. Is that what you're saying, distributes mail?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes, for instance.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: A courier within a military unit, who is a soldier, distributes mail, is that what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: Well, he doesn't just distribute mail but food or anything necessary, a piece of information or anything like that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me move to another series of questions, Mr. Rajic. I would like to move to the 19th of October, 1992. You told us that on that date you were a member of an active unit and that, in fact, you were the squad commander, and you said that you had a certain number of men under your orders; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes. On the 19th -- between the 19th to the 20th of October, 1992, I was doing a shift at Rijeka in Slatko Petrovic's house. I was performing my duty.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And your job was to be a soldier who was a member of the HVO at that time; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes. I was in the active component.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many men did you have under your command?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: I was not -- Rojnik means that I had ten people under my command, a squad.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As precisely as you can remember, what orders did you receive from your commander on the 20th of October, 1992?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: That I form a unit of 10 to 12 individuals, to form a squad. HVO troops were coming from the direction of Busovaca and Kiseljak, and they were to come to the Jajce destination, and he had heard that a barricade existed at Topola near Ahmici, and to prepare the unit if they needed reinforcements to dismantle the barricade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What equipment did you have? I'm speaking about weapons, of course.

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: We had automatic weapons.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What kind of automatic weapons did you have?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: Me personally, a Falovka .

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there other types of weapons or more powerful ones such as mortar or machine-guns?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: No. Usually they were just automatic rifles like the Kalashnikov types, 62-millimetre calibre.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did Goran Males, who you said was your friend, belong to that squad until you went to Ahmici?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: No. He didn't go with us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did Goran Males -- was Goran Males at that point a professional soldier, or in any case, on active duty?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: At that point in time, he was not. I don't remember the date he joined. He was, but not at that time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you are stating that at that date in October 1992, he was not on duty, he was not in service?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: No. No. He was not within the active component. He became included later on, but I don't know what time, exactly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Among the orders that were given to you, was there any indication of the place where you were supposed to set up in Ahmici?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Therefore, according to the orders that you were given, you were free to decide on the position that you were going to take up in Ahmici?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you very familiar with Ahmici?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: Not enough. Not sufficiently. I did know, but not enough.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: For instance, had you already gone to the forest that you indicated on the aerial photograph?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: I had not been to the forest, but I passed by the forest, because I have an aunt which lives in Nadioci, so I used to take the old railroad track, during peacetime, that is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are there several ways, several roads, in order to go from Rijeka to Ahmici?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: There is the main road, the M5 motorway; and then there's another road going via Radak's Bridge, but not directly to Ahmici. But once again it emerges on to the M5 motorway.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when you ordinarily went from your house in Rijeka to the house belonging to your aunt in Nadioci, when you did that, what was the road that you ordinarily took?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: I went on foot via Radak's Bridge, the old railroad track, the old railway line.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Mr. Usher, could we have a look at Defence Exhibit D28/5? That's the aerial photograph that we saw a little while ago.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Rajic, a little while ago you indicated a point, point 3 on the photograph, which indicates where you went with your unit. From the place which is indicated by number 3, is it possible to see the houses in Ahmici, the road, and the location where the checkpoint had been set up?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it possible from that point to see something? What can you see?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: You can see if the forces of the BH army from the direction of Kovacevac, Gornja Rovna, and Pezici, if they were to move in the direction of Ahmici and stop the blockade, the barricade which had already been set up.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If military materiel or units were set up on the main road, specifically in the area of the bus stop, from that place, what would you have seen?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You couldn't see Mehmed Ahmic's house either; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see the house after it had been damaged in the way that you described?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: Well, yes, I did, afterwards.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You answered Defence counsel's question by saying there was a shell that had caused this damage. How could you be so sure of what you are saying?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: Well, I didn't say I knew directly of that, but that I had heard that a shell had hit the house and damaged it. I didn't see it personally; I heard about it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You didn't mention that it was a shell that came from Hrasno? This is information that was given to you; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: That's right, yes, because that is where the PAT was located.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No direct knowledge of that yourself; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: I heard about it, and I knew that it had been positioned there, and that the house was hit. I could not see that at all. I just heard about it afterwards. And after things had quietened down, I passed by that area and saw what had happened, afterwards.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you specify to us at what time you arrived in that forest?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: It was about 5:30 p.m. Perhaps -- between half past 5.00 and 20 to 6.00 p.m.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us as specifically as possible, in respect of your memories, at what time you met Dragan Papic?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: Well, I wasn't looking at my watch at that time. It was between 5.00 and 5.30.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Sorry; it was "a.m.," the morning hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: It's "a.m." instead of "p.m.," Your Honour; please take note of that.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The morning hours, yes, a.m.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Until what time did you remain in that position?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: I was there until 16.00 hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: I want to go back to the transcript. It must be corrected to "a.m.," and it should not say "p.m." The correction is the opposite of what I had heard.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During that time that you spent in the woods, you told us that you were in contact through -- by Motorola with your command; did you receive instructions or orders?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: No, I didn't. In fact, when we started out, as I had the position and location, I knew my assignment, and I was told to prevent the forces of the BH army should they start moving from the direction of Gornja Rovna, Kovacevac, and Pezici towards the barricade which had already been set up by the BH army at the Topole position, or in other words, Ahmici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Under these conditions and in light of the orders that were yours, that you received and that you just recalled, are you sure that you were in the right position in the midst of that forest?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: I was not in the middle of the forest. I was in a greater depth, because we could see the whole area going towards the places that I enumerated. Because that is the only place that the forces of the BH army could pass, had they -- if they decided to move that way.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: A little while ago, you mentioned the role that was played that day by the accused Dragan Papic, and you mentioned the question of the mortar. Could you tell us whether the use of the mortar is something which the military is involved with only, or is it something which is also a prerogative of civilians?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: Well, military.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: About what you said, everything you said about Dragan Papic's activities that day, wouldn't you say that all that would lead us to think that he was exercising some kind of military activity?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: No, he wasn't engaged in military activity. In fact, he was given -- he received information while passing through Donja Rovna, I don't know who from, where to take this and to take up a position somewhere. And to fire just one shell, and that was a signal; it was just a signal that the BH army groups were drawing closer, for example, or had set out in the direction of the barricade. Because he himself was not able to do anything with that mortar.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Therefore what you're saying to us, Mr. Rajic -- I want to be very clear here, and I would like you to be as specific as possible -- is that when one arms himself with a mortar, takes a position, and fires the mortar, which might be something dangerous, this is a civilian activity. Is that what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: No, it is not civilian. I said that he was trained to do this while serving in the JNA, to perform this type of task.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you also told us, Mr. Rajic, that these were the instructions that were given to you in October, on the 20th of October, 1992.

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: I believe that Dragan told me that he received those instructions when the shooting started that evening, and I don't know who he received them from.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You're telling us that the instructions could be given to a civilian and not to a soldier, to a military person?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes, they could be given to civilians as well as to the military personnel.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does one fire a signal with a mortar? I'm just -- it's a technical question that I'm asking.

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: No, but that was -- the circumstances were such.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. I'm satisfied with that answer. Now move to the 16th of April: When you mentioned the events in Ahmici that took place on the 16th of April, 1993, you were not a witness to those events yourself, but you said -- correct me if I'm wrong, or if I interpret things incorrectly -- you told us that this was a fight between units of the Muslim army and the HVO units; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: I said that the conflict was between Muslims and Croats. Now, whether these were units, and which units, that I do not know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I won't ask you the question, then. But you also said to us that Croats had been killed in Ahmici on the 16th of April, 1993; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes, I heard that subsequently, just as I heard that a number of Muslims were killed and that a number of houses were damaged and burned down. And also that several Croats died. I don't know the exact numbers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You don't know the exact number of Croats allegedly killed in Ahmici on the 16th of April; do you know a name, the name of a Croat who was killed in Ahmici on that date?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes. For instance, Zlatko Ivankovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said -- and I hope that I'm not interpreting things incorrectly -- that during the fighting on the 16th of April, 1993, in Ahmici, the Croats in Ahmici did not take up weapons; they did not participate in fighting.

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: Would you please repeat the question? I missed the year.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: 1993. I'm speaking about the "fighting" of 16 April, 1993; that's "fighting" in quotation marks.

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes. Croats and Muslims; that is, Croat and Muslim units. But which units, how they were involved, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know whether the Croats who lived in Ahmici at that time participated in the "combat"? And I still put quotation marks around the word "combat."

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: I don't know. I don't know whether the local villagers took part in it.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: I ask your permission, Your Honour, to consult with my colleague.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the counsel please turn off their microphone?

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Your Honour, according to my colleague, I would like to go back to the -- to the events of October 1992 and ask a final question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please tell us, Mr. Rajic, at that time, if you remember, of course, at what time you received the orders telling you to prepare to go to Ahmici? Do you remember what time the orders were given?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: It was in the morning, somewhere between 5.00 and 5.05 in the morning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How were those orders given to you? Was it during a meeting or was it by telephone, on the radio?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: I received it by telephone.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As you said, was it Mr. Grabovac who gave the orders to you?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: I have no further questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Puliselic?

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: -- questions, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: All right. I assume there is no objection to the witness being released. Mr. Rajic, thank you so much for testifying in court. You may now be released. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I wish to thank you too. (The witness withdrew)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: All right. We still have 12 minutes, so probably you can bring in the next witness. (The witness entered court)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Good morning Mr. Kvasina. Could you please make the solemn declaration?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you. You may be seated. Counsel Puliselic? Examined by Mr. Puliselic:

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I will examine this witness with -- only with respect to the -- Dragan Papic's character.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Kvasina, good afternoon, sir. Good afternoon to you. Will you please introduce yourself by stating your full name, date of birth, place of birth and place of residence?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KVASINA
utterances.text: I am Dragan Kvasina, I was born on 4th of December, 1959 in Gornja Veceriska. My current residence is Gornja Veceriska in the Vitez municipality.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Since you lived all of your life in Gornja Veceriska, could you describe that area?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KVASINA
utterances.text: It is a hilly country. It is surrounded by hills and mountains, and Gornja Veceriska itself is in a sort of a vale, in a bowl, and it is surrounded by forests.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Kvasina, to your right you will see an aerial photograph of the Lasva Valley. Could you point approximately where Gornja Veceriska is? It may not be indicated on the photograph, but if you could please point us to the place. Maybe if you get up and came closer to the picture you can point to it.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KVASINA
utterances.text: Gornja Veceriska is around here somewhere (indicating).

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you very much. You may be seated.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KVASINA
utterances.text: It is around here (indicating).

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So it is not marked on the map?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KVASINA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You may sit down now. You said that it is country which is surrounded by hills and forests. What types of -- what types of woodland?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KVASINA
utterances.text: There's beech, there's birch. There's about 12 different kinds of trees. It is rich in that resource.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How far is Gornja Veceriska from Vitez if you took the road?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KVASINA
utterances.text: By road it is about seven kilometres, somewhere around there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know Dragan Papic?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KVASINA
utterances.text: Yes, I do know him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you say approximately how long have you known him?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KVASINA
utterances.text: I've known him since 1989, and I've known him well since that time and even before that I knew him slightly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you see him here in the courtroom?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KVASINA
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you say where you saw him most frequently?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KVASINA
utterances.text: Most frequently I saw him in Gornja Veceriska and in that area, sometimes in Vitez, because he was a forester up in Gornja Veceriska.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So we can say that he frequented that place regularly?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KVASINA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that he was a forester. Do you know where he worked, where he was employed, Dragan Papic that is?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KVASINA
utterances.text: He was employed in Sumarija, its Kruscica field office.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you say what did his job consist of?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KVASINA
utterances.text: His job consisted of guarding the forest in the sector where he worked, and if somebody bought the right to cut wood, then he would issue a document specifying where such a person who had come and paid would be able to go and cut wood.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that there was a lot of wood in this area. Do you know that sometimes there was some illegal logging going on and cutting?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KVASINA
utterances.text: Yes. A lot of that happened in those forests. In the area of Vitez, who -- those who did not have much money would simply go into the forest and illegally cut wood. People did it in order to survive, because sometimes winters were very harsh, you could have half a metre of snow sometimes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that people were impoverished, that they couldn't afford the basic goods let alone wood?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KVASINA
utterances.text: Yes, yes. So people just had to make do the best they could so that they could survive, simply said.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As a forester and from what you know, did Dragan Papic find these people cutting wood illegally in forests?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KVASINA
utterances.text: Yes. He occasionally would find them. And he wasn't able to protect it all. He would meet them on the roads. He couldn't cover the entire forest. For instance, sometimes he would encounter somebody on the road and sometimes in the forest.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know in such cases when he would find somebody stealing, that is, illegally cutting wood, do you know how he behaved to the people -- towards the people whom he discovered that way? Did he in some ways have understanding or was he tolerant towards them?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KVASINA
utterances.text: He was tolerant, and he behaved well to them because he understood these people. He understood that it was about their survival, because those who went to the woods were not the ones who had enough money, just those who realised that they couldn't survive without it. So he tolerated it. He would issue them warnings, and then perhaps if it's -- if it's the case that -- if it recurred 10, 20 times, then he had to report some of them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How about you, yourself? Did he ever find you cutting wood illegally in the forest? Did you also go there and illegally cut wood?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KVASINA
utterances.text: Yes, I did. I went to the forest because I had to.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You did not have money to buy wood?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KVASINA
utterances.text: No, I did not. Winters were harsh. I had to survive. I had a father and a mother, two children and a wife. Salaries were very small. They were very, very small where I worked.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When Dragan Papic found you cutting wood illegally, did he create troubles for you?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KVASINA
utterances.text: No, he did not. He warned me several times but I kept going, so on -- at one point he did report me. I understood that, because had he done that to me I would have reported him more than once. But again, he issued me a very small fine.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did the Muslims all behave in a similar fashion? In other words, did they also go and illegally cut wood in the forests?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KVASINA
utterances.text: Yes, the Muslims, Serbs. At that time we didn't make any distinctions between people with respect to the ethnic group, we were just looking at them as people. It is this war that turned everything upside down.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, what do you know about Dragan Papic? Did he treat Muslims differently, that is the Muslims who were illegally cutting wood, other than Croats?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KVASINA
utterances.text: Oh, no, he did not. He treated them equally. He was just concerned about the forest, and he did not make any distinction between Croats, and Serbs and Muslims there, nor did I ever hear that he abused or mistreated anybody along those lines.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you also see Dragan Papic in the village? Did he interact with people?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KVASINA
utterances.text: Yes, he did. When he was missing for a while, they asked, "Where is Dragan?" because he would spend some time with us in a store. We would play cards together and just sit together.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he like to make jokes and was he a social person?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KVASINA
utterances.text: Yes, he liked to joke. He would first come over and he'd say, "Where have you been? I haven't seen you in a long time." In other words, he was quite social.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Mr. President, I don't know if this is a good moment to break, because we've come to the end of this session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Yes. We'll break now and we will adjourn until tomorrow at 9.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
